reproduction_target: Comparative Tn-seq essentialome analysis of six Soft Rot Pectobacteriaceae strains using the newly developed TNSEEK pipeline (public GitLab, Docker-based): read filtering/trimming (Cutadapt) and mapping (Bowtie2) to TA-site count tables, LOESS + TTR normalization and QC (TRANSIT), HMM essential-gene classification (TRANSIT), cross-strain comparison at OMA orthogroup level and visualization; plus hybrid genome assembly (Unicycler v0.4.9) of two new genomes, OMA standalone orthology, eggNOG-mapper v2 / eggNOG v5.0 functional annotation, BLAST 2.13.0+ duplicate-gene detection, operon/polarity curation with E. coli K-12 cross-validation, Python UpSet plots, and PHASTEST prophage detection. Wet-lab work (strain growth, mariner transposon library construction by conjugation, gDNA extraction / Tn-seq library prep, Illumina NextSeq and ONT GridION sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope. Note: TNSEEK Step 4 (TRANSIT RESAMPLING for conditionally essential genes) is explicitly stated as 'not used in the present study' and is therefore excluded from the step list.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the MATERIAL AND METHODS sections 'Sequencing and genome assembly', 'Description of TNSEEK' (Steps 1-6) and 'Analysis of essential genes'. The three TNSEEK read-to-essentiality modules are kept as separate steps (C5-C7) because their parameter disclosure differs; TNSEEK Steps 5 and 6 (comparative analysis, visualization) are kept separate as C8/C9. Cutadapt and Bowtie2 are folded into one read-processing step (C5) because they are described as one pipeline stage with one shared parameter block. TRANSIT RESAMPLING (TNSEEK Step 4) is excluded: the paper states 'This step is not used in the present study'. Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted. This is a hybrid paper: it both introduces a tool (TNSEEK) and applies it to newly generated wet-lab data; routing between 'tool-methods' and 'mixed' was resolved as 'hybrid'.

steps.label: Hybrid genome assembly of P. versatile A73-S18-O15 and D. parazeae A586-S18-A17 from Illumina NextSeq 2x75 short reads + ONT GridION long reads using Unicycler v0.4.9 with default parameters (Wick et al. 2017)
Genome deposition and annotation on the NCBI platform ('The assembled genomes were deposited and annotated on the NCBI platform'; accession numbers stated to be in Table S1)
Orthologous gene matrix over the 6 genomes computed with the Orthologous Matrix (OMA) standalone package (https://omabrowser.org/standalone/, Altenhoff et al. 2019)
Functional annotation of essential genes with eggNOG-mapper v2 against the eggNOG v5.0 database (results in Table S3)

TNSEEK Step 1 - read processing: filter reads containing transposon sequence ACAGGTTGGATGATAAGTCCCCGGTCT at the 5' end, trim with Cutadapt (min transposon overlap 7 nt, max error rate 0.05, discard reads <16 or >17 nt), map with Bowtie2 end-to-end; retain only uniquely aligned reads whose 3' end is a TA dinucleotide; build raw count tables

TNSEEK Step 2 - normalization and QC: LOESS normalization for replication origin bias, TTR (Trimmed Total Reads) normalization, TRANSIT QC metrics (sum, mean, skewness, kurtosis, insertion density, QQ/QC plots) and pairwise Pearson correlation between replicate TA-sites
TNSEEK Step 3 - essential gene classification into ES / GD / GA / NE using the TRANSIT Hidden Markov Model method (DeJesus et al.)
TNSEEK Step 5 - cross-strain comparative analysis of essential genes using OMA orthogroup links to separate core, genus-specific and strain-specific essentialomes
TNSEEK Step 6 - visualization tool for individual genes / orthologous gene comparison (R Shiny + SQLite 'Discover' application; R Markdown report), producing Fig. 2 TA-site and insertion plots

Detection of gene duplications by all-against-all nucleotide similarity search with BLAST 2.13.0+ (E-value threshold 1e-5); duplicated genes excluded from the essential list and annotated ES DU (Table S3)

Operon-structure / polarity curation of TNSEEK-predicted essential genes with bioinformatic cross-validation against the E. coli K-12 essential gene set of Goodall et al.; criteria described in the Results section, no tool named
UpSet plots of shared genes and shared ES genes across the six strains generated with the Python implementation of the UpSet library (Fig. 3A/3B; display thresholds >25 genes for A and >2 for B)
Identification of intact phage regions in the six genomes with PHASTEST (https://phastest.ca/) web server

headline.static_readiness: 0/13 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: The code side is unusually strong for a Tn-seq paper: TNSEEK is a public GitLab repository (https://gitlab.cristal.univ-lille.fr/bonsai/tnseek, public, 23 commits, 1 branch, 0 tags) shipping a Dockerfile plus a pre-built image tarball, and the read-processing parameters are disclosed at an exact level (transposon sequence, overlap 7 nt, error rate 0.05, length window 16-17 nt, unique-alignment + TA 3'-end filter). The blocking gap is data: no accession (SRA/ENA/BioProject) is given anywhere for the Tn-seq FASTQ reads, nor for the Illumina/ONT reads used for the two new assemblies, and the paper carries no Data Availability section. All six TNSEEK/assembly steps that consume raw reads therefore cap at X regardless of code quality. The seven steps that operate on public NCBI genomes or on supplementary derived tables cap at NI (missing tool versions, no analysis scripts for BLAST/UpSet/curation). Even under the most generous inference-inclusive reading, the upper bound at stage 1 is 0/13 R-star with 7 NI; a stage-2 code read of the TNSEEK Docker/Dockerfile could raise the version axis on C5-C9, but those steps remain X while the input reads are undeposited.
headline.coverage: 13 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the public TNSEEK repository README/wiki prose; 5 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. TNSEEK Step 4 (TRANSIT RESAMPLING) excluded as explicitly not used in this study. The paper has no Code Availability section as such (the repository URL appears inline in 'Description of TNSEEK') and no Data Availability section at all.

gaps.where: All Tn-seq raw sequencing data (inputs to C5-C9) and the Illumina/ONT reads behind C1
gaps.missing: No sequence read accession of any kind is stated: no SRA, ENA, BioProject or GEO identifier, and no Data Availability section. The paper reports read counts (9.1-14.7 million per sample), mapping rates and insertion-site counts, but the FASTQ files themselves are not deposited or pointed to. Only the assembled genomes are stated to be on NCBI, with accessions relegated to supplementary Table S1.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the twelve Tn-seq read sets (six strains x two technical replicates) and the Illumina/ONT reads for A73-S18-O15 and A586-S18-A17 under a BioProject, and add a Data Availability statement carrying the accessions in the main text rather than only in Table S1.

gaps.where: Software environment for every named tool (C1-C13)
gaps.missing: No lockfile, conda environment, or container digest is given. The paper claims 'The complete pipeline is readily installable and executable as a Docker image' and the repository wiki instructs users to `docker build --tag tnseek -f Dockerfile` or to download https://bioinfo.univ-lille.fr/tnseek/tnseek.tar.gz, but the resulting image is referenced only as `tnseek:latest` - no digest, no version tag, and the repository has 0 git tags, so there is no immutable pointer to the environment actually used for this paper. Versions are absent for Cutadapt, Bowtie2, TRANSIT, OMA standalone, the UpSet library and PHASTEST; only Unicycler v0.4.9, BLAST 2.13.0+, eggNOG-mapper v2 and eggNOG v5.0 are pinned in prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a tagged release (or Zenodo DOI) of the TNSEEK commit used for this study and cite the Docker image by sha256 digest; record the resolved versions of Cutadapt, Bowtie2, TRANSIT, R and Python inside the image manifest.

gaps.where: C1, C10, C11, C12, C13 - the analyses performed outside the TNSEEK pipeline
gaps.missing: No scripts, commands, notebooks or configuration are provided for the Unicycler invocation, the all-against-all BLAST duplicate screen and its filtering, the operon/polarity curation and E. coli K-12 cross-validation, the UpSet plot generation, or the PHASTEST submissions. These are described only in prose and produced the curated 455/552 orthogroup sets that the paper's conclusions rest on.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit an analysis repository containing the BLAST commands and duplicate-calling filter, the curation logic (including the exact E. coli K-12 essential list used), and the UpSet plotting script, alongside the TNSEEK experimental design file used for this study.

gaps.where: C3 (OMA standalone), C7 (TRANSIT HMM), C10 (BLAST duplicate calling), C13 (PHASTEST)
gaps.missing: OMA standalone run parameters are not stated at all. The TRANSIT HMM step names the method but gives no thresholds or the ES/GD/GA/NE call criteria used. The BLAST screen gives an E-value threshold (1e-5) but no identity/coverage cutoff for declaring a duplication and no BLAST program. PHASTEST is run with unstated (presumably default) settings and no submission date, although its databases change over time.
gaps.how_to_close: State the OMA parameter file, the TRANSIT HMM settings and call thresholds, the BLAST program and duplication cutoffs, and the PHASTEST run date/version.

gaps.missing: The annotation pipeline is not named (presumably NCBI PGAP) and no version or run date is given, yet the CDS/pseudogene counts reported in the Results and the locus tags used throughout (e.g. LHK94_01575) depend on it.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the annotation pipeline and version (e.g. PGAP x.y) and the annotation release date for each accession.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: bacterial strain growth in 50% TSB at 25 C, mariner (pSamEC / himar1-C9) transposon library construction by conjugation from E. coli MFDpir, genomic DNA extraction (Wizard Genomic DNA Purification kit) and Tn-seq library preparation per Baffert et al. 2025, Illumina NextSeq 500/550 2x75 sequencing, ONT GridION 72 h sequencing
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W (5 steps), not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the bioinformatic analysis.
